revised_Text: The {{c1::pubic symphysis}} is the {{c2::cartilaginous joint}} that joins the left and right pubic bones and limits their movement.
revised_Back_Extra:
Distinguish: the pubic symphysis sits at the midline of the lowermost abdomen and closes the front of the pelvic ring, which the sacrum, ilium, ischium, pubis, and acetabulum complete.

Cue: symphysis is the general name for any joint that permits only slight motion.

why: under-clozing (R1): highlight 45 carries TWO facts — minute volume is the air moved in and out of the lungs in 1 minute, AND the equation — but only the equation is clozed, and the definition is tested by no sibling anywhere in the batch (it sits in this card's Back Extra and in card 43's Distinguish, both answer-side only). Fix: keep the whole formula in one blank per the equation recipe, but anchor it to a clozed definition sentence so both facts are tested; the Back Extra still defines each variable.
revised_Text: {{c1::Minute volume}} is the amount of air moved in and out of the lungs in 1 minute, and it equals {{c2::respiratory rate × tidal volume}}.
revised_Back_Extra:
Meaning: respiratory rate is the number of breaths in 1 minute and tidal volume is the air moved in a single breath, so their product is a volume per minute.

Pitfall: a normal rate paired with a tiny tidal volume still gives a dangerously low minute volume, so judge depth as well as rate.
